open_points.subject: Content-derived identities
open_points.text: “Submitting content whose computed identity already exists returns the existing record unchanged” does not say what happens when two unequal meanings have the same SHA-256 identity.
open_points.question: Must the kernel compare the stored meaning facts on an identity hit, and what happens if they differ?
options: Return the existing record solely by digest
Verify equality and refuse on a collision
Treat a collision as an internal fatal error
open_points.default_guess: Verify the meaning facts and stop with an internal integrity error if they differ.

open_points.subject: Sandbox determinism
open_points.text: K-05 calls admission “a deterministic verdict”, while A03 traps a closed list of clock and randomness APIs but leaves other observable nondeterminism unspecified.
open_points.question: Is determinism guaranteed for every admitted function, and if so how are unlisted sources such as other timing APIs, runtime identity, process information and standard-library entropy prevented?
options: Only the listed APIs are forbidden and determinism is best-effort
Expand isolation and traps until all supported nondeterministic sources are closed
Run repeated executions and refuse differing results
open_points.default_guess: Treat the listed traps as insufficient and close every supported nondeterministic source at the release boundary.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource outcomes
open_points.text: A03 says “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, output_bytes) — resource_exhausted” while specifying only setrlimit and parent-side counting.
open_points.question: How does the parent distinguish a caught allocation or fork failure, an address-space kill, a scratch-quota failure and an ordinary abnormal exit so the required outcome is deterministic?
options: Classify only positively observed limit events as resource_exhausted
Classify selected signals and exceptions heuristically
Add an enforcement channel that reports each limit breach
open_points.default_guess: Add parent-visible enforcement/reporting and otherwise classify an indistinguishable abnormal exit as crashed.

open_points.subject: TrialCase expected outputs
open_points.text: M06 says expected_outputs is “by output port” and may be absent, while A04 says “if the case states expected outputs, every output's digest equals the expected one”.
open_points.question: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output, or may it assert only a subset?
options: Require exactly all output ports
Allow a non-empty subset
Allow any subset, including an empty object distinct from absence
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all output ports when expected_outputs is present.

open_points.subject: Admission and activation
open_points.text: “An admitted verdict is followed at once, in the same request, by an Activation” does not say whether the verdict and activation are one store transaction.
open_points.question: Can a crash or store failure leave a durable admitted verdict without the automatic activation that submission required?
options: Write verdict and activation atomically
Permit the split state and activate on restart
Permit the split state until the implementation is submitted again
open_points.default_guess: Write the verdict and any automatic activation in one transaction.

open_points.subject: Disclosure classes
open_points.text: “An agent never receives a personal_data value” depends on classes declared by flow authors, constant authors and binding proposers, but no rule can verify that an open value is not actually personal data.
open_points.question: Is the disclosure guarantee only about declared classes, or must some trusted actor or mechanism verify the semantic correctness of those declarations?
options: Treat declarations as authoritative and scope the guarantee to labels
Require owner confirmation of every disclosure-class declaration
Introduce classification or provenance checks
open_points.default_guess: Treat declarations as authoritative and state explicitly that the guarantee applies only to correctly labelled data.

open_points.subject: Empty many-file values
open_points.text: A13 says “a file list is the elements' SpooledFiles in element order”, but an empty list has no SpooledFile carrying the list's disclosure class; the same rule requires an empty mapped result not to lower its class.
open_points.question: Where are the class and existence of an empty many-file value recorded and propagated?
options: Add list-level spool metadata
Infer the class from the producing execution and port whenever needed
Disallow empty many-file outputs
open_points.default_guess: Keep list-level transient metadata containing the port, order and disclosure class.

open_points.subject: Service credential reference
open_points.text: A17 defines “the reference that resolves to its value on the host” and later calls it a “secret file”, without defining the reference form or path-resolution rules.
open_points.question: What is a credential reference, how is it resolved, and are symlinks, relative paths, ownership, permissions, encoding and trailing whitespace allowed?
options: An absolute regular-file path with strict ownership and permissions
A path relative to the installation file
An implementation-defined host secret provider
open_points.default_guess: Use an absolute, non-symlink regular file owned by the kernel user, read as bounded UTF-8 without trimming.

open_points.subject: Installation-controlled file sizes
open_points.text: A20 says “Every global ceiling is one release constant” but defines no size limit for the configuration file, manifest records or credential files read by A16–A17 and A08.
open_points.question: What bounded read applies to each installation-controlled file, and what start or request failure occurs when it is exceeded?
options: Add explicit release ceilings for each file type
Reuse surface_request_bytes_max
Rely on unbounded filesystem reads
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit release ceilings and refuse before parsing an oversized file.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision
open_points.text: The kernel reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` “at the configured manifest_revision”, but the text does not define how a revision is resolved.
open_points.question: Does the kernel read an immutable repository object, require the working tree to be checked out at that revision, or invoke a version-control implementation, and what happens for a missing or moved revision?
options: Read the file directly from the named immutable repository object
Require manifest_location to already contain that checked-out revision
Treat manifest_revision as informational and read the working tree
open_points.default_guess: Resolve and read the file from the immutable repository object named by the revision, refusing an unknown revision.

open_points.subject: Data-directory startup
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory and everything in it are “private to the kernel's user” but does not say whether a missing directory is created or which ownership and mode combinations count as private.
open_points.question: Must the directory pre-exist, and what exact owner, group and permission checks apply to directories and files?
options: Require a pre-existing owner-only directory and files
Create a missing directory with owner-only permissions
Accept any mode with no effective access by other users
open_points.default_guess: Require or create it as kernel-owned with owner-only access, and reject every existing entry that grants group or other access.

open_points.subject: Generated service requests
open_points.text: A09 builds a request from all node inputs, but A20 defines response and per-value limits without defining a ceiling for the complete outbound request or approval preview.
open_points.question: What limits the aggregate URL, headers, JSON or multipart body, and what pre-send result occurs when that limit is exceeded?
options: Add explicit URL, header and body release ceilings
Reuse surface_request_bytes_max for the complete request
Allow any aggregate size implied by the graph
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit request-component ceilings and fail pre-send as operation_failed before writing an EffectAttempt.

open_points.subject: Service base URL
open_points.text: A08 accepts an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host, and A09 joins “the api_base_url without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”.
open_points.question: May api_base_url contain a path, multiple trailing slashes, user information, a query or a fragment, and exactly how are those cases joined?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional path without query, fragment or user information
Allow an arbitrary absolute URL and apply a specified URL-resolution algorithm
Reject every base URL whose path is not empty
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme and authority plus an optional path prefix, strip all trailing slashes, and reject user information, query and fragment.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the api_base_url host “is a loopback address”.
open_points.question: Does this include only canonical IP literals, all IP-literal spellings, `localhost`, or hostnames that resolve to a loopback address, and is the decision made before or after DNS resolution?
options: Only parsed loopback IP literals
Loopback literals and localhost
Any hostname whose resolved destination is loopback
open_points.default_guess: Accept only an IP literal that the platform IP parser classifies as loopback.

open_points.subject: TLS verification
open_points.text: A09 states only “TLS is verified for https”.
open_points.question: Which trust roots, hostname rules, protocol versions and certificate settings define verification, and may host environment variables alter them?
options: Use the operating-system trust store with pinned client defaults
Ship a release-pinned trust store and TLS policy
Use the HTTP library's environment-sensitive defaults
open_points.default_guess: Use standard hostname verification and the operating-system trust store, while ignoring environment overrides and pinning protocol policy by release.

open_points.subject: Path-placeholder inputs
open_points.text: A09 requires a placeholder input whose schema type is string or integer and at send time a “non-null string or integer”, but it does not require cardinality one and an empty string does not remain one URL segment.
open_points.question: Are many-cardinality ports and empty strings valid placeholder inputs?
options: Require cardinality one and a non-empty string or integer
Allow an empty string and send an empty segment
Allow many values by repeating or joining them
open_points.default_guess: Require cardinality one and reject an empty string at binding or pre-send validation.

open_points.subject: Multipart field names
open_points.text: A09 constructs `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`, but port names have no stated multipart-safe restriction or escaping rule.
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, controls and non-ASCII characters in port names represented without changing the declared exact headers?
options: Reject port names that are not safe quoted-string values
Apply a specified MIME quoted-string escaping
Use an extended filename/name encoding
open_points.default_guess: Reject controls and apply one specified quoted-string escaping for quotes and backslashes.

open_points.subject: Multipart approval identity
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers the “fully built request” and “Any difference at send” asks again, while A10 excludes the multipart boundary and hashes a structural list of parts so equal parts give equal descriptions.
open_points.question: Does a changed multipart boundary or wire framing invalidate an approval, or is approval intentionally over normalized multipart semantics rather than the exact body bytes?
options: Hash the exact serialized multipart bytes and boundary
Use A10's normalized part description and exempt boundary/framing differences
Make multipart serialization deterministic so both definitions coincide
open_points.default_guess: Follow A10's normalized description and explicitly exempt boundary-only framing differences while fixing one serializer.

open_points.subject: HTTP response metadata
open_points.text: A09 bounds the response body but treats malformed status lines and headers as transport outcomes without defining limits for the status line, header count or total header bytes.
open_points.question: What bounded parser limits response metadata, and how is exceeding a limit classified?
options: Add release ceilings and classify excess metadata as no valid final response
Count metadata against service_response_bytes_max
Use the HTTP library's undocumented defaults
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit release ceilings and classify an excess after sending as no valid final response.

open_points.subject: Service error failure_detail
open_points.text: A09 keeps an excerpt of an untrusted error body and classes it from the execution and declared outputs, while K-14 says an agent never receives a personal-data value and service answers are untrusted until validated.
open_points.question: How is personal data in an undeclared or invalid error body prevented from being returned to an agent as apparently open failure_detail?
options: Never expose service error-body text to agents
Treat every unvalidated service error body as personal_data
Trust the binding's declared output classes even for error bodies
open_points.default_guess: Treat unvalidated service error-body detail as personal_data for agent disclosure.

open_points.subject: Run readiness after attempts
open_points.text: A13 defines a node as ready when every input holds a value and says the next node is the smallest ready node, while waiting and retried elements can already have one or more NodeExecution records.
open_points.question: Exactly which waiting, failed, succeeded or previously attempted nodes are excluded from the ready set, and which NodeExecution determines an element's current conclusion after a retry?
options: Only an element with no current terminal conclusion and no waiting point is executable; its latest attempt controls
Any element with inputs is ready unless its node as a whole concluded
Derive state from the complete attempt history using a separately specified reducer
open_points.default_guess: Exclude every waiting or terminal element and use the highest attempt_number, modified only by A11's resolution rule, as its current conclusion.

open_points.subject: Mapped element identity
open_points.text: M20, M23, M24 and M26 use map_index, while the texts say only that elements run “in list order”; only SpooledFile list_index is explicitly “from 0”.
open_points.question: Is map_index zero-based or one-based, and is that convention shared by approvals, waiting points, executions and attempts?
options: Zero-based everywhere
One-based everywhere
Use an opaque element identifier instead of an integer position
open_points.default_guess: Use zero-based indices everywhere.

open_points.subject: Run input-set refusal
open_points.text: A12 first checks that the request “supplies exactly the flow's input ports” but does not define which mismatch is reported when ports are both missing and extra.
open_points.question: What deterministic order and distinction apply to missing versus unexpected flow input names?
options: Check missing names first, then extra names, each in code-point order
Check extra names first, then missing names
Compare the sorted supplied and required name lists and report the first difference
open_points.default_guess: Check missing required names first and then unexpected names, each by Unicode code-point order.

open_points.subject: Redacted failure_detail
open_points.text: A07 says a protected failure_detail is returned “only as its length and that class”, while A20 truncates the stored detail by UTF-8 bytes.
open_points.question: Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes or Unicode characters, and is it the original length or the retained truncated length?
options: Original UTF-8 byte length
Stored UTF-8 byte length after truncation
Stored Unicode character count after truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the stored UTF-8 byte length after truncation.

open_points.subject: Credential-header collision at startup
open_points.text: A09 says a credential header colliding with required headers “refuses to start”, but required headers come from manifest instances and the startup behavior when that manifest record or selected instance cannot be read is not stated.
open_points.question: Must startup read every configured service's manifest instance, and does a missing or malformed record stop the whole kernel or defer failure to that service's requests?
options: Validate every configured credential against the manifest and fail startup if validation is impossible
Check collisions only for readable records and defer other failures per service
Move the collision check entirely to each pre-send check
open_points.default_guess: Validate all configured credential headers at startup and fail startup when a collision check cannot be completed.
